correctness.rationale: At a polar vertex all coordinates except possibly one are signs, with the remaining coordinate determined by a tight sum constraint. In even cycle length the latter coordinate is odd, so all are signs, and there are binomial(2r,r) balanced sign choices for the active cycle roots. Omitting any one leaves a lattice basis, proving smoothness off the nonsimplicial maximal cones; the nonsimplicial points are also precisely the non-Q-factorial points. Rechecking the chart in the repair, pairing with the primitive generating roots identifies its dual lattice with the integral hyperplane of equal sign-class sums, and nonnegative exponents are generated by pairs across these classes. Pairing permutations generate the minor ideal, so this is an affine isomorphism, not a tangent-cone or finite-cover statement. The n=4 and n=6 cases give six 2×2 and twenty 3×3 cone vertices. Multiplicity is the Segre degree and the tangent dimension is r². The all-ones translation gives a principal canonical module of the Cohen–Macaulay normal semigroup ring; excellence gives normal completion. The repaired local class group calculation uses the blow-up line bundle and quotient by its zero section; its Picard group survives passage to the local base since restriction to the zero section detects it. Odd cycle maximal cones have exactly n−1 basis rays. Integral polar and primitive facet distance one give Cartier ample anticanonical divisor.
residual_risks: The class group stated is that of the local ring, not a general assertion about class groups after completion; no other lattice or fan is covered.

checked_sources: Corrected repairs/5/RESULT.md, chart and local invariants
value.rationale: On a natural nonsimplicial projective Fano family, determining that all charts are a single explicit determinantal model resolves exactly what kind of singularity the known failure of smoothness produces, in every dimension in the family. The full chart gives local equations and invariants without choosing a subdivision or passing merely to a tangent cone. The number of facets and the classical Segre invariants are not offered as separate contributions.
residual_risks: A specific complete local classification for simple cycles; neither a general toric singularity theorem nor a classification of other graph-polytope conventions.
